searchText: Feels like there needs to be incentives for geographically distant nodes to avoid clustering in the US given that the high % on aws is giving the SEC the excuse to claim jurisdiction. I think it is generally a bad idea to try to design things around the current whims of bureaucrats. They change regularly and once they decide you are within their purview, they will figure out a way to make that happen. We should focus our efforts on ensuring that it doesn't matter what regulators think because they cannot control the network. making validators earnings as constant as possible makes it so that pooling is not as important from that perspective I believe that's one way how one can help solo stakers making the operations of a node as easy and secure as possible is another Which would imply not having a plurality in a place where one call from Washington DC can shut down that much? Heck, if Amazon decided to pull a hetzner that'd be at least briefly noticeable. Even if all US validators shutdown simultaneously and never came back online, the system would still function. We would see inactivity leaks for about a month before we reach finalization, but things would autonomously self heal. Ok. <@687974325072035882> saw your msg in the other chat, but I can’t answer there. Before increasing the gas limit shouldn’t we reprice the storage opcode? We need to maintain state growth manageable The rushed merge set the precedent that $ value affects eth decisions so that means that a possible drop in $ value due to government interference should affect decisions. I would really like my bags to get bigger 😅 hasn’t been fun to watch eth take a much bigger hit than others right after the merge. If the us really goes after eth it’ll be very bad. merge was rushed in 6 years? Your mixing up what was the transition to eth 2.0 and what became the rushed merge and you are mixing eth 2 with merge? Eth 2 was the plan and then it was converted to the merge and then the rushed merge I believe? maybe? anyway, price discussion is off topic for this discord I mean if issuance and price are discussed during the eth core dev meetings as motivation for eips doesn’t it become part of r and d? no I would argue yes Though the primary thing affected by the US is centralization/freedom of the block chain which influences price so I guess that’s the main point not@price Since we do Proof-of-Stake, the price of the staked asset is important for R&D and that makes Chs2's bags value important topic? No While this point is valid, the number 32 came about to be something so that we could handle the load of the expected number of validators. That was at a price several orders of magnitude below current prices If anything it would be beneficial that price decreases so that it's cheaper to stake. ETH users/holders are not happy to hear this 😅 One should be careful to differentiate users from holders. An actor can be both a user and a holder at the same time, but need not be. Price decreases relative to <unit of account> negatively affect holders, not users. Arguably, it positively affects users due to reduction in usage costs, though this is marginal compared to gas price fluctuations. On the issue of price I have never seen a counter argument to the most naive one. I often hear that the network is unusable because of high fees. But one can argue that it's not fees that are high but that the fiat price of eth is high. The only relevant measure is the percentage of the fee with respect to the typical transaction one makes. If you needed to spend thousands of ETH to buy bread, you wouldn't mind a few Gwei spent in tx fees. Sure, we can scale, several orders of magnitude and use L2s or whatnot to lower fees, but if markets price this in and the price of eth continues to increase, then fees will again be "high" pricing out the poor. To use ETH you have to hold ETH at least for fees Also 99% of ETH users are also ETH holders that hold more than just for fees We dont discuss about price here And I honestly dont care that much either, as of now. Yes, if price goes up, it would be nice but it is not my personal priority right now Maybe i am the only one with this feeling Reminder: This server isn't the right place to talk about geopolitics or the actions, behaviors, or statements of various governments. No. Ethereum is censorship resistant regardless of where people run their nodes. This is very intentionally designed. If a > 33% of validators suddenly go offline the chain will stop finalizing, but it will self heal eventually. While undesirable, it is working as intended and there is nothing additional we need to do from a technical standpoint to address it. The problem is already accounted for and coded against. Validating is intentionally made to be relatively easy, so a person can simply start validating from another location if their location goes offline (though, take care to protect against double-signing if you are moving to a new machine without cleanly shutting down the first!) We'd like to move chaindata/ancient from SSD to HDD (raid, striped). Will that negatively impact geth's operation? Please redirect if this is the wrong channel. <@526093370066731048> You will not be able to achieve the IOPS required to keep up with the chain. I believe that state retrieval is the bottleneck. I naively tried running Geth on an SSD L2ARC-cached ZFS pool on RAIDZ2. That quickly failed. Also this is probably off-topic here. There is a Geth developer discord. But I can't see a #users channel there, so I assume that it's dev only. Moving ancient to HDDs will not negatively impact performance (unless you are heavily relying on fetching it via RPC) Don’t forget that all slots that were delegated to AWS US East will be missed which will negatively impact block times (and thus throughput) Also, non-finalization will put a lot of stress on CL So you guys should definitely work on ensuring that Ethereum doesn’t get concentrated in us-east-1 And FWIW “self healing” is weeks if not months (if someone can confirm exact duration, that’d be perfect) This should provide an incentive to run your validator from somewhere that isn't AWS East. More generally stakers should aim to run their validators in a way that avoids correlated failures with other validators. The penalties for uncorrelated failures are much more minor than correlated ones.
